# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

## From cand_0001 (tau2 airline, tool-surface edit space)
- Un-fixable-by-design failures pollute the target set. Tasks whose terminating user turn carries ###STOP###/###TRANSFER### end the sim before the agent can emit any write call, so NO tool body ever executes — the tool-surface edit space provably cannot move them (here: 17, 19, 22 = 3 of 8 failures). The proposer wastes reasoning ruling them out. Suggestion: the harness could pre-classify and flag such tasks (e.g. "terminated before agent's final action") in INSTRUCTIONS.md / trajectories, or exclude them from the "failures to fix" list when the chosen edit surface cannot reach them, so breadth effort concentrates on reachable clusters.
- A tiny, sanctioned verify sandbox would help. I hand-wrote a scratch harness that stubs the frozen env_* primitives and execs each tool body on exact trace args to prove FIRES-on-failing / NO-OP-on-passing. This is the single highest-value safety step for multi-edit candidates. Shipping a first-class helper (a `verify_tool(tool, args, stub_env)` utility + the passing/failing arg fixtures already extractable from trajectories) would make the REAL+SAFE+VERIFIED discipline the default rather than something each proposer reinvents.
- The passing-task args needed for the SAFE check aren't handed over directly. I reconstructed task 25's exact book args from the trajectory to prove a no-op; providing the recorded tool-call args for currently-passing tasks alongside the failing traces would make regression-proofing faster and less error-prone.
